clue.text: It's meant to be the finish of a' race

definitions.text: It's meant to be the finish of a' race

parts.words: It's meant to be the finish of a' race
parts.note: reads like something planned as the end of a running contest, but race here means a people, and the deed is a deliberate attempt to wipe one out

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a finishing line; 'race' is an ethnic group and 'finish' its destruction.
explanation.definitionFit: Mass killing intended to exterminate a whole people is exactly what the word names.

clue.text: Walk slowly up to get past .a' lemur

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for dawdling is read upwards

parts.note: to lag is to fall behind or walk slowly
ago means in the past

explanation.surface: Someone strolls up to get past a lemur at the zoo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' reverses LAG to GAL; 'to get' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The bushbaby is a small African primate of the lemur-like prosimian group.

clue.text: A gaol isn't free from homesickness

indicators.note: the letters are set free to form a new order

explanation.surface: A prisoner insists prison does not cure homesickness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' rearranges A GAOL ISNT; 'from' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Wistful longing for home or the past is the sense of homesickness.

clue.text: Tart in a cooking dish

definitions.meaning: an old word for a prostitute or loose woman

explanation.surface: A pastry tart baked in an oven dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tart' is not pastry but the French term for a prostitute; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: The French word names both a kept woman and a small ovenproof pot.

clue.text: Note signal to rise by a quarter to two

parts.note: D is a musical note

indicators.note: in a down clue the word for a signal goes upwards

parts.note: a cue is a signal to act
E for east, one quarter of the compass

explanation.surface: A musical note signals a rise of a quarter at a quarter to two.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to rise' turns CUE into EUC; 'by' joins on E (east).
explanation.definitionFit: In cards and dice the two is called by this name.

clue.text: Joris, Dirck and.I all went at this

definitions.text: Joris, Dirck and.I all went at this

parts.words: Joris, Dirck and.I all went at this
parts.note: Joris and Dirck are the riders in Browning's poem How They Brought the Good News from Ghent to Aix, who with the narrator rode at full speed all the way

explanation.walkthrough: Browning's poem opens 'I sprang to the stirrup, and Joris, and he; I galloped, Dirck galloped, we galloped all three'.
explanation.definitionFit: The fastest pace of a horse is the one the three riders kept up throughout the poem.

clue.text: Having no bristles, unlike Jaques's pard

definitions.meaning: lacking the bristly beards on ears of grain
in As You Like It, Jaques describes the soldier as bearded like the pard, so unlike it means beardless

explanation.surface: Something smooth, unlike the bearded leopard of Shakespeare's speech.
explanation.walkthrough: Jaques's 'seven ages' speech in As You Like It has the soldier 'bearded like the pard' (leopard); awns are the beards of grasses.
explanation.definitionFit: Awns are the beard-like bristles on cereal grains, so lacking them is beardless.

clue.text: Gamble recklessly and lose pawn in forward movement

indicators.note: the chess piece's letter is to be dropped from the word

parts.note: to plunge is to bet heavily
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A chess player gambles and loses a pawn in an attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link; the chess surface hides a fencing thrust.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden thrust forward, as in fencing, is a forward movement.

clue.text: Excuse to celebrate? That's. nice

parts.note: a plea is an excuse offered
to sing is to celebrate in song

explanation.surface: Any excuse for a party is welcome.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to' and 'That's' are links.
explanation.definitionFit: Something agreeable or gratifying is nice.

clue.text: Shilling basket has broken leg to contend with

parts.note: S is the abbreviation of the old British shilling
a trug is a shallow wooden garden basket

indicators.note: the letters of the limb are broken into a new order

explanation.surface: A cheap basket with a broken leg is a nuisance to cope with.
explanation.walkthrough: A TRUG is a shallow British garden basket; 'broken' turns LEG into GLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To fight or strive hard is to contend.

clue.text: Drop features and get embarrassed

definitions.meaning: read literally, to mislay one's face or facial expression
to be put out of composure, abashed

explanation.surface: Someone's face falls as they become flustered.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half reads the phrase literally: 'countenance' is the face, so losing it is dropping one's features.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to lose composure or be abashed; taken word by word it means to mislay one's face.

clue.text: Recipient's word of: surprise about tirade

indicators.note: the exclamation sits around the outburst, so one word goes about the other

parts.note: gee is an exclamation of surprise
a rant is an angry tirade

explanation.surface: Someone receiving a gift exclaims in surprise at a torrent of words.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Recipient's' stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone to whom something is formally granted, such as land or funds, is a recipient of it.

clue.text: Advice to the immoderate and vain'

definitions.meaning: read as two words, telling an excessive person to consume less

explanation.surface: Telling the greedy to cut back is a waste of breath.
explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer is an instruction to the excessive: use less.
explanation.definitionFit: Effort in vain is futile, of no avail; split, the word is a command to consume less.

clue.text: Regina, eg, to change at one

indicators.note: the letters of the queen's title and the abbreviation are to be altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A queen, say, is being made to alter her position.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to change' rearranges REGINA and EG together.
explanation.definitionFit: Being at one with someone means being in accord, sharing the same view.

clue.text: Very personal hint

definitions.meaning: as a verb, to suggest indirectly

explanation.surface: A private clue passed between friends.
explanation.walkthrough: The adjective and the verb are spelt alike but said differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means close or private; the verb means to suggest indirectly.

clue.text: Car — old single-seater

definitions.meaning: an American term for a saloon car
the enclosed chair carried on poles by two bearers in past centuries

explanation.surface: A vintage car with room for only the driver.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is the sedan chair, a seat for one carried by porters in the 17th and 18th centuries.
explanation.definitionFit: A saloon motor vehicle in American usage, and a carried chair for a single passenger in history.

clue.text: Talked at length, but not enough in fact

indicators.note: the scarcity word sits in the fact word

parts.note: a deed is an act or a legal fact
scant means insufficient

explanation.surface: Someone spoke for ages yet said little of substance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but' is a link; 'fact' is DEED, as in 'in deed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To descant is to discourse at length on a subject.

clue.text: Cables to change and check

indicators.note: the letters are changed into another order

explanation.surface: An engineer is told to replace the wires and inspect them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'change' rearranges CABLESTO; 'and' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A hindrance or barrier holds back progress, as a check does.

clue.text: Perch round the king? Cheek!

indicators.note: the fish's name goes round the royal letter

parts.note: the bass is a spiny fish of the perch family
R, from Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Someone resents an upstart perching beside the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Perch' is not a seat but a fish; BASS goes round R (Rex).
explanation.definitionFit: Effrontery or nerve, as in 'the brass neck to ask', is impudence.

clue.text: Silver a school accepted for putting away

indicators.note: the school takes in the metal, holding it inside

parts.note: Stowe is an English public school in Buckinghamshire
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: A school took in a silver donation for safekeeping.
explanation.walkthrough: Stowe is a well-known English fee-paying boarding school, so 'a school' is a specific one rather than a general word; 'accepted' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Stowing goods away, as in a ship's hold, is putting them away.

clue.text: A setter, one involved in formal composition

indicators.note: the letters are tangled together into a new order

parts.note: the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A crossword compiler takes part in writing a formal essay.
explanation.walkthrough: 'involved' rearranges A SETTER with I (one).
explanation.definitionFit: A systematic written discourse on a subject is a formal piece of writing.

clue.text: Shine like Carroll's bat

definitions.meaning: in Alice in Wonderland the Hatter sings 'little bat, how I wonder what you're at'

explanation.surface: Lewis Carroll's bat glows in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hatter parodies the nursery rhyme as '..., little bat'.
explanation.definitionFit: To sparkle or glint is to shine, and that is what the Hatter's bat does.

clue.text: If you say it's a ram that's. not productive

indicators.note: spoken aloud the word for if sounds like the sheep

parts.note: whether means if

explanation.surface: A ram that will not breed, if you ask.
explanation.walkthrough: 'you say' signals the sound; 'it's a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A castrated male sheep cannot sire lambs.

clue.text: After "Othello", prompt return to the bar!

indicators.note: the joined words are read backwards
the second word is placed after the first

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's Moor of Venice
pat means timely or ready, as in a pat reply

explanation.surface: After seeing Othello, a theatregoer hurries back to the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: MOOR then PAT, read backwards whole by 'return', gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A pub room where beer is served from casks is a bar.

clue.text: Put in a spot

explanation.surface: Something put in a spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link between the verb and noun senses.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb it means to set down; as a noun, a location or position.

clue.text: What-is certain to 'happen about uniform in a sloop

indicators.note: destiny's word is placed about the clothing word

parts.note: fate is what is destined to occur
rig is outfit or costume

explanation.surface: Destiny catches up with a sailor in uniform aboard a small warship.
explanation.walkthrough: FATE goes about RIG; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Both are sailing warships; the setter takes the vessel loosely as a kind of small man-of-war.

clue.text: Drive violently about in front

indicators.note: the abbreviation sits in the front word

parts.note: fore means front, as in to the fore
c for circa, about

explanation.surface: Driving recklessly round at the front of the pack.
explanation.walkthrough: C (circa) goes in FORE.
explanation.definitionFit: To compel or push by strength is to drive violently.

clue.text: Personal description, of sorts, by Jack

parts.note: printers' sorts are pieces of type, each one a letter or symbol
Jack Ketch was a notorious 17th-century English hangman

explanation.surface: Someone sketches a vague portrait of a person, drawn by a friend called Jack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of sorts' looks like a vague hedge but means pieces of type; Jack is the hangman Jack Ketch, whose name became slang for any executioner. 'by' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A short written portrayal of someone's personality is a description of a person.

clue.text: This used to attract a plus in an examination

definitions.text: This used to attract a plus in an examination

parts.words: This used to attract a plus in an examination
parts.note: refers to the old British school test taken at about that age, whose name added a plus to the number

explanation.walkthrough: The British eleven-plus was an exam taken at about age eleven to decide on grammar-school entry.
explanation.definitionFit: The number is the first part of the name of the former selective school exam, followed by 'plus'.

clue.text: Back causes delay round goal

indicators.note: the delaying verb goes round the aim word

parts.note: to defer is to postpone
an end is an aim or goal

explanation.surface: A slow full-back holds up play around the goalmouth.
explanation.walkthrough: In football or hockey a back is a defensive player.
explanation.definitionFit: A full-back or back in team sport is a defensive player.
